q: How coal-heavy are East and West Godavari refractory units, and is there a loan route?
title: Godavari refractories: coal and ADEETIE
short: Almost entirely coal: 9,882 of the cluster's 9,940 toe goes into downdraft kilns, roughly 40,000 t CO2 a year, about 0.64 t per tonne of refractory. Both districts are on BEE's ADEETIE list, so a loan for a kiln upgrade that saves at least 10% energy can earn interest subvention.
audience: Refractory units in Rajahmundry, Morampudi, Dhavaleswaram, Chebrolu, Bhimdole and Dwarka Tirumala

ul: 19 units in East Godavari and 7 in West Godavari make about 62,530 t a year, worth about Rs 36 crore.
Almost all fire in downdraft kilns of 40 to 250 t a batch. Green ware dries in the open, so most kilns stop in the monsoon.
Coal of 4,000 to 4,800 kcal per kg comes largely through a state quota from Singareni. Units say quota coal is poor and they burn more of it; open market coal is better but dearer.
Energy is 40 to 45% of the cost of a tonne.

p: The average unit burns 380 toe of coal and 26,145 kWh a year; the range runs from 164 to 977 toe. Firing takes 6.66 GJ per tonne of product.

sections.h: The loan route, step by step
ol: Check you qualify: Udyam registration and manufacturing inside the named cluster.

Pick the upgrade: the cluster profile points to dampers, coal sizing and feeding, kiln temperature indicators, flue gas preheating, and in time a tunnel kiln. BEE's technology list is open, so these can be proposed.
Build a baseline from 12 months of coal bills, electricity bills and tonnes fired, so the empanelled auditor can size a saving of 10% or more.
Borrow Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore; micro and small units get 5 points off the interest rate, medium units 3, with the net rate floored at 2%.

p: Subvention is paid each year the saving holds, so log coal per tonne fired every month. A wet season with fewer firings should not look like a lost saving.

example.title: One unit's baseline (estimate)
lines: Coal: 380 toe x 10 million kcal / 4,400 kcal per kg = about 864 t
Output: 62,530 t / 26 units = about 2,405 t, so 0.64 t CO2 per tonne
A 10% coal saving: 86 t of coal, about 152 t CO2 a year
example.note: Energy and output from the 2019-20 cluster profile; coal tonnes assume the middle of the reported heat value range. Use your own coal bills.

senseible: Senseible reads twelve months of coal invoices and electricity bills into a dated baseline with CO2, the starting point an auditor needs before sizing the 10% saving.
